title: Measurement of mitochondrial respiratory chain enzymatic activities in Drosophila melanogaster samples
protocol: Homogenize samples in 2-3 mL of MS buffer with BSA, using 15-20 strokes at 1,000 rpm in a motor-driven Teflon-glass Elvehjem potter on ice.
Transfer the homogenate to a clean 30 mL centrifuge tube.
Rinse the potter with 7 mL of MS buffer with BSA and transfer to the tube containing homogenate.
Centrifuge the homogenate at 1,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Filter supernatant through a 100 μm strainer and transfer it into a new tube.
Centrifuge samples at 6,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove lipids adhering to the tube walls during washing steps.
Discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet with 10 mL of MS buffer containing BSA.
Repeat the previous centrifugation step.
Resuspend the pellet with 10 mL of MS buffer without BSA after discarding the supernatant.
Centrifuge samples at 7,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 300–400 μL of MS buffer without BSA.
Measure protein concentration using a method of choice (e.g., Bradford, Lowry, or BCA).
Set up measurements in triplicate to ensure consistency and reliability.
Store samples at −80°C for no more than 3 months to avoid multiple freeze-thaw cycles.
Pellet isolated mitochondria by centrifuging samples at 7,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the pellet with hypotonic buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.6) to achieve a final protein concentration of 1 μg/μL.
Snap-freeze the sample in liquid nitrogen.
Thaw the sample at 25°C in a benchtop thermo shaker or, alternatively, in a water bath.
Perform three freeze-thaw cycles to enhance mitochondrial membrane disruption.
Keep samples on ice during enzymatic activity assays.
Use a plate reader for kinetic activity measurements if a 96-well plate is used.
Register absorbance values every 20 or 30 seconds for 2 minutes, depending on the number of samples and reading speed.
Warm reaction buffers to 20°C–25°C before starting assays.
Measure enzyme activities at least in triplicate.
Include at least one replicate reaction in presence of a selective inhibitor to calculate specific activity.
Conduct complex I (NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase) activity measurements at 30°C.
Add 186 μL of the reaction mix into each well of a 96-well plate using a multichannel pipette.
Add 10 μL of mitochondrial lysate (1 μg/μL) and mix well.
Record baseline activity at λ=340 nm for 2 min at 30°C.
Add 4 μL of 4 mM CoQ1 to each well to start the reaction.
Mix well in the reaction mix.
Promptly record absorbance at λ=340 nm for 2 min at 30°C.
Prepare the reaction mix as described.
Add 196 μl of the reaction mix into each well of a 96-well plate.
Add 2 μL of mitochondrial lysate (1 μg/μL) and mix well.
Shake the plate for 5 s.
Pre-incubate the plate at 25°C for 10 min.
Record baseline activity at λ=600 nm for 2 min at 30°C.
Add 2 μl of 4 mM CoQ1 (final concentration 40 μM) to each well to start the reaction.
Shake the plate for 5 s.
Record absorbance at λ=600 nm for 2 min at 30°C.

Shake the plate for 5 s, wait for 5 s.
Record baseline activity at λ=550 nm within 2 min at 30°C.
Add 2 μL of 10 mM decylubiquinol to each well to start the reaction.
Shake the plate for 5 s.
Wait for 5 s.
